footerNote: Cloudflare reports a single operating segment. Chart note: Cloudflare's running costs exceeded its gross profit; other income covered nearly all of the gap, so the chart draws the remaining $1.29M net loss as a 'Covered by cash on hand' source, which also covers the $3.14M tax bill.

oneTimers: Stock-based compensation and related employer payroll taxes totaled $119.699M in Q3 across cost of revenue and operating expenses — the main reason GAAP shows an operating loss while non-GAAP operating income was $85.938M.
Amortization of acquired intangible assets was $3.699M in Q3 — also excluded from non-GAAP results.
No one-time charge landed in Q3 itself: the $3.840M lease impairment and the $15.000M one-time compensation charge in the nine-month figures fall outside this quarter.
otherDetail: Interest income of $42.529M, less $2.912M of interest expense and $0.307M of other expense, net — total non-operating income of $39.310M.

segments.name: Cloudflare platform
segments.note: All of Cloudflare's revenue — its connectivity cloud platform for making websites, applications and networks faster and more secure. Cloudflare reports as a single operating segment, so this is the total revenue; up 31% YoY.

takeaways.text: Revenue hit $562.0M, up 31% YoY from $430.1M a year ago. Management said growth accelerated for the second consecutive quarter, and remaining performance obligations — work customers have already committed to — grew 43% YoY, with current RPO up 30%.
takeaways.title: Growth accelerated for a second straight quarter

takeaways.text: GAAP loss from operations was $37.5M, or 6.7% of revenue, versus a $30.8M loss a year ago. But $39.3M of non-operating income — mostly $42.5M of interest income — nearly wiped it out, leaving a net loss of just $1.3M versus $15.3M a year ago. Excluding stock-based compensation of $119.7M and other items, non-GAAP operating income was $85.9M.
takeaways.title: Nearly breakeven despite a GAAP operating loss

takeaways.text: Dollar-based net retention was 119%, up from 110% a year ago, meaning existing paying customers spent 19% more than they did a year earlier. Large customers — those paying over $100,000 a year — rose to 4,009 from 3,265, and paying customers overall grew 33%.
takeaways.title: Existing customers keep spending more

verdict: Cloudflare grew revenue 31% to $562M and nearly broke even on a GAAP basis — a net loss of just $1.3M — as $39.3M of mostly interest income offset a $37.5M operating loss, while existing customers expanded spending at a 119% retention rate.
